name: Iran MuddyWater — MERCURY / Static Kitten
author: Threat Intelligence Team
prerequisites: PowerShell ScriptBlock logging (Event 4104) enabled via Group Policy
Endpoint EDR covering all Windows systems
Proxy/web gateway logs capturing application-layer HTTP metadata
Network flow data available for the hunt window
required_tools: Splunk or Elastic with Windows Event, proxy, and network log indexes
Sysmon with process creation (Event 1) and network connection (Event 3) logging
EDR console (CrowdStrike, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint)
CISA Advisory AA22-055A IOC list loaded into SIEM

hunt_actions.title: Legitimate RMM Tool Abuse Detection
actions: Hunt for unauthorized Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tools — MuddyWater abuses ScreenConnect, RemoteUtilities, Syncro, and Atera as C2: `index=windows EventCode=4688 Image IN (*ScreenConnect*,*RemoteUtilities*,*Atera*,*Syncro*,*AnyDesk*,*TeamViewer*,*Zoho*) | stats count by host, Image, CommandLine | where NOT [search index=approved_software tool_name IN (*ScreenConnect*,*RemoteUtilities*,*AnyDesk*)]` — any RMM tool not in the approved software inventory is a finding

Detect RMM C2 callback traffic to unapproved cloud relay infrastructure: `index=proxy cs-uri-stem IN (*screenconnect.com*,*remoteutilities.com*,*syncromsp.com*,*atera.com*) | stats count by src_ip, cs-uri-stem, cs-username | where NOT [lookup approved_rmm src_ip OUTPUT authorized | where authorized='yes']` — relay connections through approved RMM vendors from unapproved endpoints are equally suspicious

hunt_actions.title: PowerShell-based Persistence and C2 (POWGOOP, CANOPY)
actions: Hunt for POWGOOP DLL loader (loads PowerShell-based malware via regsvr32): `index=windows EventCode=4688 (Image=*regsvr32.exe* CommandLine=*/s* AND CommandLine!=*ScrRun.dll*) OR (ParentImage=*regsvr32.exe* Image=*powershell.exe*) | table _time, host, Image, ParentImage, CommandLine` — POWGOOP uses regsvr32 to load a DLL that spawns an obfuscated PowerShell C2 loop

Detect CANOPY data collection script (collects system info, exfils via HTTP POST): `index=windows EventCode=4104 ScriptBlockText=*Get-WmiObject* AND ScriptBlockText=*Invoke-WebRequest* AND ScriptBlockText=*POST* | table _time, host, ScriptBlockText` — CANOPY fingerprints the victim host and sends results to C2; look for WMI queries combined with outbound HTTP POST in the same PowerShell session

hunt_actions.title: Log4Shell Exploitation for Initial Access
actions: Hunt for Log4Shell exploitation attempts against internet-facing Java applications (MuddyWater actively exploited CVE-2021-44228): `index=webserver (uri_path=*${jndi:* OR uri_path=*${${lower:j}ndi* OR user_agent=*${jndi:* OR user_agent=*${${::-j}${::-n}${::-d}${::-i}*) | table _time, host, c-ip, cs-uri-stem, cs(User-Agent)` — also check HTTP request headers (X-Forwarded-For, User-Agent, Referer) as Log4Shell payloads were inserted into all header fields

Identify post-exploitation activity following Log4Shell (MuddyWater deployed web shells and reverse shells): `index=webserver sc-status=200 cs-method=POST cs-uri-stem IN (*/.*/,*/tmp/*) | stats count by cs-uri-stem, c-ip | where count > 5` — also: `find /opt /var/www /usr/local -name '*.class' -newer /etc/passwd -ls 2>/dev/null | grep -v '.jar' | sort`

hunt_actions.title: Scheduled Task and Registry Persistence
actions: Hunt for MuddyWater scheduled task persistence (uses schtasks.exe with obfuscated PowerShell): `index=windows EventCode=4698 | rex field=TaskContent '<Command>(?P<cmd>[^<]+)' | where match(cmd, 'powershell|wscript|cscript|mshta|regsvr32|rundll32') | table _time, host, TaskName, cmd, SubjectUserName` — MuddyWater scheduled tasks typically use encoded PowerShell or VBScript and run as SYSTEM

Detect registry run key persistence with obfuscated commands: Sysmon Event 13 (RegistryValueSet): `index=windows EventCode=13 TargetObject IN (*\CurrentVersion\Run*,*\CurrentVersion\RunOnce*) | where match(Details, 'powershell|wscript|cscript|rundll32|mshta|regsvr32') | table _time, host, TargetObject, Details, Image` — compare registered values against known-good software baseline

questions: Is there a formally maintained and enforced approved software list, and are unauthorized Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tools blocked from execution via AppLocker, WDAC, or EDR policy?

Are all internet-facing Java applications (including Atlassian, VMware, Cisco products) patched against Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) and subsequent Log4j vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-45046, CVE-2021-45105)?
Is PowerShell ScriptBlock logging (Event 4104) and Constrained Language Mode enforced organization-wide to limit MuddyWater's ability to execute arbitrary PowerShell payloads?

Are outbound connections from servers to Remote Desktop / RMM relay infrastructure (e.g., ScreenConnect cloud, AnyDesk relay nodes) monitored and alerted upon if the connection was not pre-approved via change control?
Are scheduled task creation events (Windows Event 4698) monitored in the SIEM with alerting for tasks created outside of approved maintenance windows or by non-administrative accounts?
Is regsvr32.exe execution by standard user accounts or from non-standard directories (e.g., Temp, AppData) blocked via application control policy?

Are CISA advisories for MuddyWater/MERCURY (AA22-055A and subsequent updates) reviewed upon release, and are associated IOCs ingested into the SIEM and endpoint security tools within 24 hours of publication?

Are government-sector and telecommunications partner organizations included in the threat model for this assessment, given MuddyWater's documented targeting of these sectors in the Middle East, Europe, and North America?
